summary: ISO 68-1 basic-profile derivation of M2.5 x 0.45 reproduces the published table: d2 2.207716 (published 2.208), d3 1.947909 (1.948), D1 2.012861 (2.013), As 3.390804 mm2 (3.39, delta 0.000804). The coefficients 0.649519 / 1.226869 / 1.082532 are computed from H = P*sqrt(3)/2 inside compat.thread_geometry(), not typed in, so the agreement is an independent check and not a restatement. Same derivation shape as threaded-m2 row 0001, at the M2.5 size.
by: claude (microduck lane C, electronics verification), compat.py run under python3 stdlib

summary: ISO 261 coarse pitch for nominal 2.5 mm is 0.45 mm and this connection encodes 0.45. Cross-checked against ce-cad/cecad/fasteners.py line 58 M2.5 row (pitch 0.45, tap 2.05, close clearance 2.70, normal 2.90, loose 3.10, cbore 5.2) and against the workshop shelf's ce-parts/screw-m2.5-iso4762 (ISO 4762 length family, 14 lengths verified on a fetched page). compat.compatible() FAILs any pair declaring a different pitch, including M2.5 x 0.35 fine; mate.py refuses it too — watched refusing in its __main__ self-test 2026-09-03, four deliberate breaks, four refusals.
by: claude (microduck lane C), read from cecad/fasteners.py line 58 and ce-parts/screw-m2.5-iso4762

summary: WHERE THE M2.5s ARE, measured not asserted. SPEC.md section 4's hole census over Pollen's meshes counts a fourth population the M2 row does not explain: Ø2.7/2.8 x20, which are the fasteners.py M2.5 close (2.70) and normal (2.90) clearances, and docs/BOM.md section 4 buys M2.5x6 x20 for them. Two subsets are measured directly: the three head-close screws, Ø2.695 clearance + Ø5.500 x 2.824 counterbore into Ø2.100 x 11.200 printed posts with a Ø2.800 x 0.800 lead-in (out/verify/manufacturing_partial.json, bottom_head_shell / top_head_shell); and the four compute-board mount holes, Ø2.8140 sd 0.0125 measured off Radxa RAD-DOC-0084 Rev 1.10 section 4 by tools/measure_radxa_drawing.py (part:radxa-zero-3w). Ø2.814 gives 0.314 mm diametral clearance on M2.5 against 0.814 mm on M2.
by: claude (microduck lane C), SPEC.md section 4 + out/verify/manufacturing_partial.json + part:radxa-zero-3w cad/interfaces.json

summary: TIGHTENING TORQUE, PRELOAD AND PLA PULL-OUT ARE NOT KNOWN and are not being estimated. The torque-preload relation is implemented in compat.preload_from_torque() with NO default for mu_thread, mu_bearing or d_km_mm (same refusal as threaded-m2 row 0004 and threaded-m3 row 0004 - an assumed mu moves the answer more than 2x). The M2.5 case adds the same second gap the M2 one has: the head-close joint forms its own thread in a printed PLA post (Ø2.100 measured) and no pull-out or strip torque of such a joint has been measured in this workshop. A bench pull-out with a scale would close this row and earn T2. Anisotropy makes it worse here than for M2: top_head_shell slices dome-up so the layer planes are perpendicular to the post axis and pull-out is inter-layer-bond limited.
